title: Runtime Confidence Lab: Fidelity Probes and SLO Slicing
author: Jordan Li
content:
Summary
------
This page documents the Runtime Confidence Lab: an integrated laboratory protocol for (A) probing model fidelity under production-like degradations, (B) exercising kernel hinting and scheduler signals, and (C) slicing SLOs to estimate graceful-degradation envelopes. The goal is a repeatable playbook teams can run prior to rollouts, kernel changes, quantization updates, or routing policy changes.

Scope
-----
Applies to: runtime-agent (serving runtime), kernel-mapper, fidelity-orchestrator, and the benchmarking harness. Intended for: runtime engineers, performance SREs, model-onboarding, and platform QA.

Motivation
----------
Production incidents often arise at the intersection of fidelity regressions and scheduler changes. A single experiment run should answer: 
- How does model output fidelity (task-specific metrics) vary as we induce latency/capacity constraints?
- Which kernel hints (tensor-layout / attention-splitting) materially change latency vs. fidelity trade-offs?
- What SLO slices become brittle under co-tenancy or tail-load conditions?

High-level concepts
-------------------
- Fidelity probe: a deterministic workload of representative prompts and reference outputs used to measure quality (BLEU / ROUGE / task-specific scoring + open-ended heuristic checks).
- Kernel hinting: explicit scheduler metadata we expose to the kernel-mapper to bias execution paths (e.g., fast-path, memory-saver, quantized-eager).
- SLO slicing: partitioning traffic by features (seq_len, model_variant, tenant_tier) and measuring SLO attainment per slice.

Lab prerequisites and hardware/software matrix
--------------------------------------------
Use one of the approved lab stacks below; attach the telemetry snapshot prior to running experiments.

| Stack name | GPU | OS | Runtime image tag | Notes |
|------------|-----|----|------------------|-------|
| lab-small  | A10G| Ubuntu 22.04 | runtime:v2026-05-10 | single-node baseline |
| lab-large  | H100| Ubuntu 22.04 | runtime:v2026-05-10 | multi-GPU topo with nvlink |
| edge-sim   | T4  | CentOS 8     | runtime:v2026-05-10-edge | simulates constrained memory |

Minimum software: benchmarking harness >= 1.14.0, profiler-agent >= 0.9.3, kernel-mapper >= 2.3.0.

Baseline thresholds (for our standard open-model ensemble)
-------------------------------------------------------
| Metric | Baseline | Alerting threshold (soft) | Failure threshold (hard) |
|--------|----------|---------------------------|--------------------------|
| p50 latency (ms) | 45 | 80 | 150 |
| p95 latency (ms) | 110 | 200 | 400 |
| token cost (uUSD/token) | 0.003 | 0.006 | 0.01 |
| task-fidelity (task-F1) | 0.92 | 0.88 | 0.84 |

Experiment matrix (cross-product)
---------------------------------
1) Workload shapes: short-chat (avg seq 80), doc-gen (avg seq 600), multimodal-sim (50% short tokens, 50% long)
2) Kernel hints: fast-path, memory-saver, quantized-eager, default
3) Degradations: cpu bottleneck (throttle worker), nvlink degradation (drop 30% bw), eviction-pressure (fill 85% GPU mem), increased burst traffic (2x arrivals for 5m)
4) Model variants: baseline-fp16, q4f-compat, trimmed-llm-small

Procedure (step-by-step)
------------------------
1. Environment prep (10–20 minutes)
   a. Snapshot current telemetry: curl -sS http://telemetry.internal/snapshot > telemetry-prior.json
   b. Deploy experiment image: kubectl apply -f overlays/experiment-profile.yaml --record
   c. Ensure kernel-mapper is at the target version: kubectl set image daemonset/kernel-mapper kernel-mapper=kernel-mapper:2.3.0

2. Baseline run (30 minutes)
   a. Run the harness in baseline mode: bench-harness run --config experiments/baseline.yaml --out out/baseline.json
   b. Collect profiler traces: profiler capture --interval 30s --out out/baseline.trace
   c. Validate baseline fidelity: python tools/score_fidelity.py --pred out/baseline.pred --ref gold/fidelity-corpus.json --report out/baseline.score.json

3. Kernel-hint sweep (per hint, 20 minutes each)
   For each kernel hint in [fast-path, memory-saver, quantized-eager, default]:
   a. Apply hint: runtime-agent ctl set-kernel-hint --hint <HINT> --selector test-cohort
   b. Run harness with same workload: bench-harness run --config experiments/short-chat.yaml --hint <HINT> --out out/hint-<HINT>.json
   c. Record traces and fidelity scores.

4. Degradation runs (30–60 minutes each)
   a. Induce degradation using chaoskit: chaoskit inject --scenario nvlink-drop-30 --target cluster-lab-large
   b. Re-run the harness for the workload shapes and model variants.

5. SLO slicing simulation (automated, 45 minutes)
   a. Use slo-slicer tool to partition results: slo-slicer ingest --results out/*.json --slices "seq_len,tenant_tier,model_variant" --out out/sliced-report.json
   b. For each slice, compute violation risk: python tools/slice_risk.py --input out/sliced-report.json --thresholds configs/slo-thresholds.yaml

Data collection and artifact naming convention
--------------------------------------------
- Artifacts should be stored under s3://redwood-lab/runtime-confidence/<run-id>/ and follow naming:
  - <run-id>-metadata.json
  - <run-id>-traces.tar.gz
  - <run-id>-bench-results.json
  - <run-id>-fidelity-report.json

Profiling and telemetry configuration
-----------------------------------
Recommended profiler flags for fidelity experiments:
- profiler-agent --sampler stratified --rate 20Hz --kv-annotate --capture-kernel-calls
- Enable syscall-level tracing only when reproducing kernel handoff problems (adds 10–15% overhead)

CLI snippets (examples)
----------------------
# Baseline harness run
bench-harness run --config experiments/baseline.yaml --out out/baseline.json --concurrency 64

# Kernel hint set
runtime-agent ctl set-kernel-hint --hint fast-path --selector test-cohort

# Start SLO slicer
slo-slicer ingest --results out/*.json --slices "seq_len,tenant_tier,model_variant" --out out/sliced-report.json

Analysis checklist (what to look for)
------------------------------------
- Fidelity drift vs baseline: absolute drop > 0.03 (task-F1) is a red flag.
- Latency/fidelity covariance: if p95 latency rises and fidelity drops together, suspect contention or passive throttling.
- Kernel hint sensitivity: >15% p95 difference between hints indicates kernel path bifurcation.
- Cost delta: token cost change > 10% requires product review.

Runbook: when an experiment flags a regression
-------------------------------------------
1. Re-run with deterministic seed and single-tenant isolated node.
2. Capture full profiler traces and kernel-mapper logs: kubectl logs -l app=kernel-mapper --since=1h > out/km.logs
3. If hint-dependent: revert to previous hint for canary and open ticket with kernel-mapper (owner: eng-serving-runtime/kernel-team).
4. If eviction/frag-related: run gpu-memory-fragmentation-diagnostics-playbook and schedule compaction window.
5. Create postmortem entry with artifacts link and severity tag.

Release notes template (for kernel or runtime changes validated by this lab)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Change: kernel-mapper 2.3.0
- Verified: baseline p95 latency change: +4ms (p50 +2ms), fidelity change: -0.005 task-F1
- Experiments run: baseline, fast-path, quantized-eager, nvlink-drop-30
- Canary recommendation: enable fast-path for dedicated tier only; monitor slice: seq_len>512, tenant_tier=free

Known issues and mitigations (collected)
-------------------------------------
1. Non-deterministic fidelity drops with quantized-eager on q4f-compat
   - Symptom: intermittent hallucination on long-context doc-gen
   - Mitigation: hold quantized-eager behind feature flag; run extended fidelity regression for 24h before rollout
2. Kernel hint not honored under high eviction pressure
   - Symptom: trace shows fallback to default kernel path when global mem > 90%
   - Mitigation: add preflight check in runtime-agent to fail fast and mark node degraded
3. SLO-slicer undercounts slices when requests lack seq_len metadata
   - Symptom: slice misattribution in multi-tenant traces
   - Mitigation: update ingress processors to populate seq_len header (task: ENG-6543)

Ownership and escalation
------------------------
- Experiment owner: eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking (primary)
- Kernel hint triage: eng-serving-runtime/kernel-team (primary), eng-sre (secondary)
- Fidelity regressions: applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding (primary)

Appendices
---------
A. Example experiment config (YAML)
------------------------------------------------
# experiments/short-chat.yaml
workload:
  name: short-chat
  concurrency: 64
  sequence_length: 80
model_variant: baseline-fp16
prompts: corpora/short-chat-1000.json
metrics:
  - latency_ms
  - fidelity_task_f1
  - token_cost

B. Quick checklist before PR merge
- [ ] Bench harness passes in CI (golden-run)
- [ ] Baseline fidelity within 0.01 of production baseline
- [ ] Kernel-mapper is covered by unit tests for hint handling
- [ ] Profiling flags documented in PR
